title: Elton John Dusts Off Rare 1969 Gem 'Skyline Pigeon' at Rock in Rio
summary:
Elton John has a legendary catalog of hits, but some of his best songs are the ones he rarely plays. On September 8, 2026, at Brazil's Rock in Rio festival, the music icon treated fans to a rare live rendition of "Skyline Pigeon," a deep cut from his 1969 debut album Empty Sky. It was the first time he'd performed it since 2019.

"This next song is the first good song I wrote with Bernie [Taupin]," John told the enthusiastic crowd. "And Brazil is the only place it's ever been popular, so here we go."

The song's journey is fascinating. Initially, Empty Sky was a commercial flop, and "Skyline Pigeon" went largely unnoticed. But after John's breakthrough in 1970, fans rediscovered it. In 1972, he and his band re-recorded it during sessions for Don't Shoot Me I'm Only the Piano Player and released it as the B-side to "Daniel." That version ended up on a Brazilian soap opera called Carinhoso, turning it into a surprise hit in Brazil. That's why most of his 17 previous live performances of the song took place in Brazil, Ecuador, or Chile.

John has a deep emotional connection to the song. Its lyrics—"Turn me loose from your hands, let me fly to distant lands"—evoke themes of freedom and release. In 1990, he sang it at the funeral of Ryan White, a young man who died of AIDS, and later explained to NPR that the song's message about "release and freedom" felt appropriate for the occasion.

Since wrapping his massive 330-date Farewell Yellow Brick Road tour in July 2023, John has stepped back from full-time touring but continues to play select events. He's also working on a new album, with Bernie Taupin revealing that John has been collaborating with producer Andrew Watt and others. "It's a whole different ballgame for him," Taupin said.

For fans at Rock in Rio, hearing "Skyline Pigeon" live was a magical moment—a rare glimpse into the early days of a legend's career, delivered with the warmth and showmanship that have made Elton John a beloved figure for over five decades.
why_it_matters: A song's meaning can change when people connect it to their own culture or to grief, as 'Skyline Pigeon' did through a Brazilian soap opera and a funeral. For young audiences, the story shows that music history is shaped not just by the charts but by memory, place, and the emotional moments when a song is played.

background_read: Elton John (born Reginald Kenneth Dwight) is an English singer and pianist; he and lyricist Bernie Taupin had already begun their five-decade partnership when they made Empty Sky, the 1969 debut album that launched John's career.
The record sold poorly at first, but after John's mainstream breakthrough in 1970, listeners and radio programmers started digging into his early songs.

In the 1970s music industry, vinyl singles had an A-side for radio promotion and a B-side that was often treated as a throwaway, yet media exposure on TV soap operas could still turn a B-side into a regional hit.

Ryan White was an Indiana teenager with hemophilia whose HIV infection from a blood transfusion made him a national symbol during the early AIDS crisis; John had become his friend and sang at his funeral in 1990.

Rock in Rio, one of the largest music festivals in the world, has hosted everything from Brazilian pop to international rock stars and remains a place where artists can play songs tied to personal memory and meaning.

perspectives.perspective: Positive — fans at Rock in Rio
perspectives.description: Fans heard a song most concertgoers never get a chance to experience live. John's warm performance turned a lesser-known track into a shared, emotional moment, especially because he explained why Brazil mattered to the song.

Concert tours increasingly depend on nostalgia, with legacy artists playing their oldest material rather than taking creative risks. While rare gems like 'Skyline Pigeon' are special, there is a risk that newer songs get lost if audiences only reward the past.

The song's strange path from a flop album to a Brazilian hit shows that commercial success is often accidental and regional. B-sides, soap operas, radio playlists, and live setlists all shape which songs survive in the public memory.

perspectives.perspective: Forward-looking — those watching John's next chapter
perspectives.description: John has stepped back from full-time touring, but he is working on a new album with producer Andrew Watt and longtime lyricist Bernie Taupin. The challenge will be to honor his beloved past while also giving the next album a real chance to find its own unexpected fans.
